subject: Nexus AI — Request for tri-region dedicated slices and onboarding timeline
summary: Prospect asks for dedicated GPU slices in US/EU/APAC aligned to deal milestones; internal asks for sizing, lead times, and onramp cadence. Agreed MLP: start with burst-able reserved slices in US + EU, pilot APAC micro-pool, SOW and traffic forecast attached.
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex.park@nexusai.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: capacity@nexusai.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU slices for Nexus launch (US / EU / APAC)

Sergio — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Nexus is targeting an enterprise launch in November and we need clarity on a dedicated capacity plan across our initial geos. High-level ask:

- Reserved slices: steady-state baseline for US (prod) and EU (prod) with burst capacity for major customers.
- APAC: pilot micro-pool (Singapore) with ability to scale to reserved if demand justifies.
- Rough lead times (procurement -> reserved capacity live) and minimum commit tiers.

I attached a short forecast and a draft SOW (pdf). Can you loop in the capacity folks and provide an activation matrix and timeline we can share with our ops team? We prefer a canary first-week and then a wider rollout.

Appreciate it — alex

Attachments: nexus-onramp-traffic-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), Nexus_MAL-SOW_v1.pdf (attachment stub)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Alex Park <alex.park@nexusai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU slices for Nexus launch (US / EU / APAC)

Alex — great to meet yesterday, thanks for the materials. Looping Lauren (sales ops) to capture commercial floor and Hannah (capacity) for sizing / lead times.

High level next steps from our side:
1) Hannah to propose a tri-region activation matrix (baseline + burst + pilot) with estimated GPU-count and expected latency SLOs by region.
2) Lauren to confirm minimum commit tranches and earliest go-live dates by tranche.
3) We’ll draft a Milestone Action Plan (MAP) aligned to your November target.

Can you confirm whether Nexus needs dedicated NVMe-backed KV cache persistence or if ephemeral cache is acceptable for the first 30 days? That affects node sizing.

— Sergio

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated GPU slices for Nexus launch (US / EU / APAC) — proposed activation matrix

Folks — reviewed Nexus forecast and sketched an initial activation matrix. Key assumptions: 1) mixed-batch + streaming workloads with median seq len ~512, 2) prefix caching desirable but non-blocking for MVP, 3) traffic peaks coincide with PST business hours and EU evenings.

Proposal (summary):
- US (prod): start with 12 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (2x6 nodes for HA), burst pool +6 GPUs for first 3 months. Lead time: 4–6 weeks to provision and validate.
- EU (prod): 8 A100-eq reserved (2x4), burst +4. Lead time: 5–7 weeks (scheduling + compliance checks).
- APAC (pilot): 3 A100-eq micro-pool (single AZ Singapore), pre-warm cache nodes for canary. If 30‑day pilot shows >2x baseline usage, convert to reserved 6 GPUs (lead time 6–8 weeks).

Notes and open questions:
- If Nexus requires NVMe-backed KV persistence for cold-start reduction, add +1 GPU per 4 reserved GPUs to offset I/O-bound tail latencies.
- Quantization profile: recommend int8 for US/EU to reduce unit cost; APAC pilot can stay float16.
- Can we get Nexus to accept a 3-month initial tranche for US + EU to accelerate provisioning? That lowers lead time.

I attached the sizing sheet (derived from their forecast) as a reference.

— Hannah

Attachments referenced: sizing_table_nexus_v1.csv (internal spreadsheet note)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Alex Park <alex.park@nexusai.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU slices for Nexus launch (US / EU / APAC)

Alex — thanks, quick commercial follow-up.

- Minimum commit: standard tranche = 3-month reserved block (billing monthly) per region. We can progressively convert APAC pilot to a reserved tranche with 30 days notice once metrics cross the threshold.
- Pricing: I’ll send a formal quote but ballpark: US reserved block (12 GPUs) discounted vs on-demand; EU similar with a small regional premium; APAC pilot priced as ephemeral reserved pilot.
- Contracting/Procurement: we can accept Nexus PO + SOW signature. For faster provisioning we recommend preliminary acceptance of SOW and an initial non-binding allocation hold while contracts complete.

If that commercial model works, Sergio / Hannah — can we confirm a provisional activation timeline for Nexus (canary start Oct 15, phased roll Nov 1)? Alex — are those dates workable on your side?

— Lauren
